comparison: Perfect agreement on motif enrichment analysis (C32-C35, C58-C62). Both evaluations find the TEAD1 motif enrichment findings well-supported by systematic analysis across independent cell types. OpenEval emphasizes methodological rigor with HOMER/CisBP, while peer reviewers accept findings without challenge.

Perfect agreement on GWAS enrichment findings (C13, C47-C48, C102-C103, C113, C148). Both evaluations support the connection between TEAD1 disruption and developmental phenotypes. OpenEval highlights statistical rigor and replication across phenotypes, while peer reviewers accept the findings as thoroughly presented.

Agreement on uncertain status of C66 regarding functional impact of H3K27ac reduction on enhancer activity. OpenEval notes the claim is speculative and correlation-based, requiring additional functional experiments. Peer reviewers similarly note incomplete demonstration of functional consequences.

Strong agreement on ATAC-seq data quality and chromatin accessibility findings (C2-C3, C30-C31, C49-C51). OpenEval emphasizes specific QC metrics (FRiP >0.5, TSS enrichment >30), while peer reviewers praise technical reproducibility and comprehensive approach. Peer result also includes HiChIP claims (C52-C55) not in OpenEval R1.

Agreement on HiChIP data quality (C52-C55). OpenEval provides detailed quality metrics (67% valid pairs uninfected, 52% infected) and validation approaches. Peer reviewers affirm the looping data as convincing within their broader evaluation of chromatin data.

Agreement on ChIP-seq findings showing TEAD1 binding reduction (C36, C64, C68, C70-C72). OpenEval emphasizes dramatic quantitative changes (75,554 to 17,567 peaks) and statistical significance. Peer reviewers affirm integrative ChIP-seq data as convincing and note functional data was added in revision.

Partial overlap on integrative chromatin analysis (C4-C8, C73-C75). OpenEval focuses on hierarchical model with specific loci examples. Peer result R3 covers broader ChIP-seq claims including C36-C38, C64-C65, C68-C72 not in OpenEval R6, but shares support for integrative chromatin findings.

Agreement on integrative conclusion about TEAD1 role (C8, C46). OpenEval supports hierarchical model through multi-dataset integration. Peer reviewers accept TEAD1's role in cellular response to HCMV infection, noting the work presents important information on TEAD1 disruption.

Agreement on RNA-seq and pathway analysis (C76-C80, C82). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance of TEAD1 reduction (3.7-fold, p=1.9×10^-29) and pathway enrichment. Peer reviewers accept transcript-level changes and Western blot validations, with broader claim coverage including C84-C86, C115, C117, C125.

Agreement on YAP1/pYAP1 reduction mechanism (C10, C43, C88-C89, C95-C96). OpenEval provides specific p-values and notes inference about pYAP1 is reasonable but not definitive. Peer reviewers accept Western blot validations within broader mechanistic evaluation covering C9, C11-C12, C42, C44-C45, C92-C93, C98-C99, C101.

Agreement on TEAD1 transcript and protein reduction (C11, C44, C82, C92). OpenEval emphasizes concordance between RNA-seq and Western blot data. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of comprehensive mechanistic validation.

Agreement on alternative splicing findings (C12, C45, C98, C101). OpenEval notes functional consequence relies on literature citation rather than direct demonstration. Peer reviewers accept RT-PCR validations within broader mechanistic evaluation.

Agreement on chromatin accessibility mechanism (C9, C42, C70). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance of co-occurrence (p=1.4×10^-215). Peer reviewers accept this mechanism within comprehensive validation including Western blots and RT-PCR.

Agreement on TEAD1 target protein reduction (C84-C86). OpenEval views this as functional validation of TEAD1 activity reduction. Peer reviewers accept Western blot validations of downstream targets within broader gene expression evaluation.

Partial agreement on H3K27ac changes (C65, C69). OpenEval notes global reduction p-value (p<0.19) doesn't reach significance, weakening the claim, though ChIP-seq peak reduction is robust. Peer reviewers accept H3K27ac findings within integrative chromatin evaluation without noting statistical limitation.

Agreement on CTCF stability as control (C67). OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates specificity to TEAD1 rather than global transcription factor disruption. Peer reviewers accept this comparative finding supporting focus on TEAD1.

Divergence on integrative conclusion (C116). OpenEval supports the multi-mechanism model with convergent evidence but notes causal relationships not quantitatively established. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether TEAD1 disruption is direct consequence of infection or secondary to innate response, noting TEAD1 overexpression doesn't substantially impact replication.

Partial overlap on C117. OpenEval supports integrative conclusion synthesizing multiple approaches. Peer result R5 accepts gene expression findings broadly but doesn't specifically address the integrative synthesis that OpenEval R19 emphasizes.

Agreement on alternative splicing of TEAD1 exon 2 (C99). OpenEval notes functional significance unexplored and minimal discussion. Peer reviewers accept splicing findings within comprehensive mechanistic validation.

OpenEval supports control findings showing expected enrichments for other transcription factors (C56-C57). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these control analyses.

OpenEval supports integration of current findings with prior literature for biological context (C104-C109, C111-C112). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this literature integration, though peer R7 accepts GWAS connections.

OpenEval rates speculative claim about broader viral strategy (C137) as UNCERTAIN, noting it's a hypothesis for future testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this speculative extrapolation.

Peer reviewers support TEAD1 specificity among TEAD family and CTCF stability (C63, C67). OpenEval R14 addresses C67 separately, but C63 (TEAD1 specificity among family members) appears in OpenEval R5 and R9 contexts rather than as standalone evaluation.
